question: According to the Census of India 2011, what is the share of workforce engaged in the agriculture sector?
solution:
The correct answer is __**54.6%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to the Census of India 2011, the share of the workforce engaged in the agriculture sector was 54.6%.
 
• This figure includes both cultivators (those who own or lease land and are engaged in cultivation) and agricultural laborers (those who work on other people's land for wages).
 
• The agriculture sector remains a significant employer in India, especially in rural areas.
 
• However, this percentage represents a decrease compared to the Census of 2001, which recorded 58.2% of the workforce engaged in agriculture.
 
• This decline indicates a gradual shift of the workforce towards other sectors of the economy, such as industry and services, due to urbanization and better employment opportunities.
 
• Despite the decrease in the percentage, the absolute number of agricultural workers still remains substantial in India.
 
• The agricultural workforce plays a crucial role in food production and the overall economy of the country.
 
• The contribution of the agriculture sector to India's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) has also been evolving over the years.
 
• While the share of the workforce in agriculture is high, its contribution to the GDP is comparatively lower, highlighting issues related to productivity and income in the sector.
 
• The Census data provides valuable insights into the occupational structure of the Indian population and the distribution of the workforce across different sectors.
 
• Understanding the trends in the workforce engaged in agriculture is important for policy formulation related to rural development, employment generation, and agricultural reforms.
 
• The migration of agricultural labor from rural to urban areas in search of better economic opportunities is a contributing factor to the changing workforce composition.
 
• Government initiatives and policies aim to modernize agriculture, improve productivity, and enhance the income of those engaged in the sector to address these shifts.
